title: Senior Solution Support Engineer
description:
**About the Role:**
GSK’s Enterprise AI team is expanding its ability to architect, build, and run complex AI solutions across the enterprise. Senior Solutions Engineers sit at the intersection of technical architecture, hands-on AI engineering, and production operations — ensuring that AI capabilities translate reliably into production value and keep delivering it after go-live.
  
  
As a Senior Solutions Engineer you will own the technical solution design for complex AI integrations and personally build and operate them, working across EAI engineering, business technology teams, external partners, and strategic suppliers to ensure that what gets built can be deployed, integrated, maintained, and operated at enterprise scale. This is a hands-on role: you will design, build, and review AI systems yourself — including LLM, agentic, and retrieval-based solutions — working within the architectural standards, engineering practices, and lifecycle framework set by the Staff Solutions Engineer, and contributing to how they evolve. You bring both the architectural depth to make the right design choices and the communication skills to earn confidence across technical and business audiences.
  
  
The role carries direct accountability for the AI products and integrations you deliver. Expect to spend roughly 40% of your time on production operations and support — keeping the lights on (KTLO), meeting SLAs and service metrics, and day-to-day coordination with strategic suppliers — and roughly 60% on engineering, with a deliberate focus on using that engineering to automate operations and steadily reduce the operational load.
  
  
You will use AI agents as part of your engineering and operations toolkit, supervising their output, to keep lowering the cost at which value is delivered for the solutions you own. As those solutions scale in deployment, you are responsible for identifying when the current engineered solution needs to be refactored and/or optimised, and for recommending and delivering that change — escalating portfolio-level cases to the Staff Solutions Engineer.
  
  
**Why This Role Exists:**
As the Enterprise AI portfolio matures, the complexity of integration, deployment, and operations grows. Many of the most valuable AI opportunities require deep technical solutioning before engineering can begin, hands-on engineering to build them, and disciplined operation once they are live. In this role you will be the person who:
  
  

* Closes the gap between AI capability and enterprise deployment readiness through rigorous technical solutioning.
* Enables faster delivery by resolving integration complexity early, before it becomes a production blocker.
* Builds and ships production AI solutions hands-on, so that architectural decisions are grounded in working code rather than slideware.
* Keeps products healthy in production by owning KTLO, SLAs, and service metrics for the solutions you deliver.
* Automates the run through monitoring, AIOps, and AI agents, so reliability improves and the cost to operate falls as the portfolio grows.
* Governs the lifecycle by applying Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) discipline — stage gates, versioning, change control, and traceability — to every AI product you deliver.
* Raises the bar on solution quality by applying and contributing to architectural standards across complex engagements.
* Builds trust with business technology partners and enterprise architects through credible, well-grounded technical guidance.

**Key Responsibilities:**
**Solution Architecture & Technical Design**

* Own technical solution design for complex AI integrations — from requirements through to detailed architecture, component selection, and integration specification.
* Define integration patterns for connecting AI capabilities with enterprise systems: SAP, Veeva, Salesforce, clinical data platforms, and GSK’s data infrastructure.
* Design for operability so that observability, SLOs, runbooks, and support requirements are built into the solution from the start rather than added after go-live.
* Produce solution architecture documentation that enables downstream engineering teams to build with confidence and minimises ambiguity at handoff.

**Hands-On AI Engineering (approx. 60% of role)**

* Build and ship production AI solutions — including LLM-based applications, agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and ML model serving — integrated with GSK enterprise systems.
* Write production-quality code and reference implementations, with tests, evaluation harnesses, guardrails, and CI/CD for the AI systems you deliver.
* Apply the function’s AI engineering standards — prompt and model versioning, evaluation, secure deployment — and contribute improvements back to them.
* Evaluate models, frameworks, and tooling through hands-on benchmarking of quality, latency, cost, and risk, and recommend the right choice for each engagement.
* Partner with Forward Deployed Engineers and platform engineers to take proven prototypes through to hardened, supportable production services, and own the handoff for your engagements.
* Use AI agents and coding assistants as part of daily engineering and operations, supervising and quality-assuring their output to lower the cost of delivering the solutions you own.

**Deployment Readiness & Technical Assurance:**

* Lead technical due diligence for complex deployments — identifying integration risks, data dependencies, security considerations, and operational requirements before build begins.
* Drive deployment readiness assessments ensuring AI solutions meet enterprise architecture standards, security policy, and regulatory requirements prior to production.
* Provide technical assurance throughout delivery — reviewing design decisions, flagging architectural drift, and escalating risks to engineering and product leadership.

**Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) for Enterprise AI:**

* Apply the PLM framework and stage gates to every AI product and integration you deliver, preparing the release evidence — evaluation results, security, data privacy, regulatory and quality requirements.
* Maintain accurate lifecycle records for your products — models, versions, prompt versions, dependencies, owners, and status — and drive change management, deprecation, and retirement.
* Ensure traceability and auditability across the lifecycle (data lineage, model and prompt versions, approvals, and decisions), suitable for a regulated pharma environment.
* Feed delivery and operational experience back into the PLM framework so that gates and criteria improve over time.

**Production Operations & Support (approx. 40% of role):**

* Own production operation and support for the AI integrations and products you deliver, including KTLO activities such as patching, upgrades, dependency and certificate management, and break-fix.
* Deliver against SLAs, SLOs, and service metrics (availability, latency, incident response and resolution times, change success rate, cost to serve) for your services, reporting performance to the Staff Solutions Engineer and business owners.
* Diagnose and resolve integration failures and lead incident response for your services, running post-incident reviews that drive root-cause fixes rather than repeated manual remediation.
* Work day to day with strategic suppliers and platform vendors on delivery — raising and tracking tickets, coordinating support escalations, and flagging performance or SLA issues to the Staff Solutions Engineer.
* Maintain runbooks and knowledge base articles for your services, and participate in the on-call and escalation model.
* Track operational toil for the services you own and convert it into automation.

**Intelligent Operations & Automation:**

* Build and operate observability for your services — monitoring of model quality, drift, hallucination and safety signals, latency, availability, and cost — with defined SLOs, alerting, and runbooks (AIOps / LLMOps / MLOps).
* Apply AI and agents to operations itself — automated triage, root-cause analysis, runbook execution, cost and capacity optimisation, and self-service support for product teams.
* Feed production usage and operational data back into design, evaluation, and PLM decisions so the portfolio improves with every release.
* Contribute to operating-model standards — ownership, support tiers, escalation, and the FDE-to-SE handoff — drawing on what you learn running real services.

**Solution Evolution & Cost-to-Value:**

* Track unit-economics and value metrics for the solutions you own (for example cost per transaction or outcome, and run cost against business value) and use them to prioritise optimisation work.
* As your solutions scale in deployment, identify when the current engineered solution needs to be refactored and/or optimised — for performance, reliability, cost, or maintainability — and make the case, plan the work, and deliver the change; escalate portfolio-level cases to the Staff Solutions Engineer.
* Monitor scale signals (usage growth, latency, cost per unit, incident trends, architectural limits) so that refactor and optimisation decisions are triggered early, and feed the outcomes into reusable patterns.
* Own the technical roadmap for integration capabilities, identifying where investment in common patterns will reduce cost and risk across the portfolio.
* Contribute to platform engineering decisions based on deployment and integration experience — feeding real-world constraints back into how the platform evolves.

**Partner Engagement & Technical Governance:**

* Represent EAI’s technical architecture in conversations with enterprise architecture, data governance, security, and vendor partner teams.
* Build and maintain relationships with business technology leads across GSK to support alignment and accelerate approval of complex deployments.
* Contribute to EAI’s technical standards and architecture decision records, ensuring decisions are well-reasoned, documented, and reusable.

**Required Experience:**

* 15+ years in enterprise solution architecture, software or AI engineering, or technical pre-sales/post-sales engineering, with a track record of designing complex integrations.
* Recent, hands-on AI engineering experience: you have personally built and deployed production AI/ML or LLM-based systems (for example RAG, agentic workflows, model serving, evaluation pipelines) and can write, review, and debug code in languages such as Python.
* Strong working knowledge of enterprise integration patterns, APIs, event-driven architectures, and data exchange standards.
* Practical experience with MLOps/LLMOps and cloud-native deployment (CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code, observability) sufficient to make sound decisions about AI deployment, integration, and operability.
* Experience supporting production operations for enterprise platforms or AI services, including KTLO, SLA/SLO and service-metric delivery, incident and problem management, and on-call or escalation models.
* Experience using automation — and ideally AI agents — to reduce operational toil and the cost of delivery or operation.
* Working knowledge of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) or equivalent lifecycle governance for technology, data, or AI products, including stage gates, versioning, change control, and retirement.

* Track record of recognising when a system needs to be refactored or optimised as it scales, and delivering that work (performance tuning, re-architecture, cost optimisation).
* Experience operating in a regulated enterprise environment (pharma, healthcare, or financial services preferred).
* Confidence engaging with senior technical and business stakeholders: running workshops, producing crisp architecture artefacts, and defending design choices.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Experience in an AI-native company or equivalent AI-first engineering environment.
* Familiarity with ITIL or SRE practices (error budgets, blameless post-incident reviews, change management) applied to AI and data platforms.
* Familiarity with GxP, computer system validation, or other quality and regulatory frameworks as they apply to AI and software products.

Our mission is to turn millions and billions of raw, fast-moving event streams from multiple systems into a single, trustworthy Mobility + Platforms data lakehouse that every analyst, data scientist, and ML engineer etc at Uber depends on.
  
  
A Senior Staff Data Engineer on this team is the person trusted to lead these initiatives for the Mobility Org at Uber.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* As a Senior Staff Data Engineer, you are an organization-level technical leader, not just for one team, but for the Mobility + Platform data ecosystem as a whole. You set multi-half-to-multi-year direction, force-multiply dozens of engineers across teams you don't directly manage, and are trusted to point Uber's technical investment in the right direction with real autonomy.
* Architect the data lake/lakehouse strategy for Mobility + Platform
* Own data modeling and schema design for core mobility entities that dozens of downstream teams build on; this role is explicitly weighted toward deep data modeling and SQL mastery over general-purpose application coding.
* Set the technical vision and strategy for an entire portfolio of data platform investments (governance, schema registry, pipeline health/SLAs, backfill tooling, validation frameworks) rather than executing a single project; identify ambiguous, org-wide data problems before they're obvious to others.
* Build and scale the pipelines and infrastructure (batch and streaming) that keep petabyte-scale mobility data fresh, reliable, cost-efficient, and auditable.
* Drive data governance and quality as a first-class engineering discipline.
* Mentor and uplevel Staff and front-line engineers and EMs across multiple teams; act as a technical thought partner
* Partner cross-functionally with Mobility Science, Fares, Matching, Fulfillment, and platform teams to align the mesh of embedded and central data engineering work.
* Represent data engineering in org-wide planning, advocating for and securing investment in projects with outsized, multi-team business impact; think in terms of large-scale transitive impact, not single-team wins.
